extracted.intended_audience: high-school journalism students / student newspaper reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for student reviewers reporting on books, plays, films (silent and sound), and musical performances; aimed at teaching how to gather facts, judge quality, and write vivid, responsible reviews for school/local papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid writing and engaging openings
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the reviews in this chapter. Find evidences of vivid writing. How do the opening paragraphs excite your interest?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work for grace of style in book reviewing. Use devices that secure vivid, smooth writing and vivid, forceful writing; craft openings to immediately excite reader interest. (Exercises prompt clipping examples and imitating effective openings.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer shows knowledge beyond the book
rubrics_metrics.description: How do the reviews in this chapter show the reviewer to have a knowledge that extends beyond the confines of the book reviewed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate background and context — relate the work to other works, genres, authors or historical/literary context to show informed judgement rather than isolated opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague generalities; support claims with specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Here is a poor review. Why is it poor? Go over it, making all abstract or vague terms concrete. Support general statements by specific references to the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make abstract assertions concrete with quotations, plot examples, or references to scenes/lines. If you have not read the work, indicate where improvement is needed and state its nature rather than speculating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide bibliographic/classification and contextual info
rubrics_metrics.description: Give information as to type of play, dramatist, producer, cast, place of production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always supply readers with necessary identifying details (type/genre, author/dramatist, production credits, cast, place and date of production; for books include title, author, publisher). This orients the reader and grounds critical comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground judgments in the work and its type
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for judging plays must be found in the play; therefore, students intending to review a play should inform themselves on the types of plays and the essential qualities of a good play in each type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess according to standards appropriate to the play's genre/type rather than imposing unrelated criteria. Know what constitutes success for comedies, dramas, mysteries, one-acts, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four elements to consider in play reviews
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly treat each element: the script and dramatic content (Play), the staging/design/directorial choices (Production), performers' interpretation/skill (Acting), and the audience's reception and responsiveness (Audience). Which element you emphasize depends on the play's particular interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate how production and acting affect the play
rubrics_metrics.description: A poor play is often saved by perfect acting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether acting or production enhances or redeems weaknesses in the script; note when acting or staging is the dominant reason to see (or avoid) a production.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-school review scope and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: The high school review is not expected to be the review of a first night performance. The young reviewer should write up the play as a project in composition. His review may influence student attendance at the production if it is timely enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the practical limits of student reviewers: focus on clear, timely reporting suitable for the school community; first-night insider claims are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand scenario technique and film standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Before attempting to review a film the student should know something of scenario technique, for a film must be reviewed in the light of film standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquire basic knowledge of film storytelling and technical conventions (scenario, montage, shot composition) so criticism can assess how well the film meets its medium-specific standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include film production credits and adaptation source
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers of a film review will want to know the place of production, the producer, the cast, the writer of the scenario and the titles, with the book and the author from which it was made, if adapted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List production details and adaptation pedigree to inform readers of provenance and to frame commentary about fidelity or interpretation when a film is based on preexisting material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key considerations for film reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider: Film. Production of it. Characters and their acting. Titles. Relation of film to book from which taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure film reviews to address the film as story/artwork, production values (direction, cinematography, editing), performances, inter-titles or dialogue, and how the film compares to its literary source if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound-film technical and performance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the points for comment under the silent film, consider: Kind of sound film: all talkie, part talkie, sound picture. Perfection of mechanical devices for producing natural voice effects. Timing of action to sound devices. Diction of actors: pronunciation, enunciation, articulation. Relation of sound to the movement of the play. Appearance of actors from legitimate stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For talking pictures assess technological execution (clarity, synchronization), how sound integrates with visuals and pacing, and actors' vocal technique and suitability to screen sound; note special issues for part-talkies or transitional forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate cinematic technique, atmosphere and photographic effects (silent film)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess camera technique, use of shadows, lights and photographic angles to create atmosphere; note forceful camera effects and atmospheric mood as part of film's artistry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on director/cinematographer choices (angles, lighting, shadow, montage) and whether these techniques serve story and mood; cite exemplary sequences (e.g., evocative camerawork or set pieces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective musical performance reporting; facts first
rubrics_metrics.description: He can give an objective report of a musical performance within his limitations and add his own impression. Such comment must be to the point and in the light of the facts of the performance. There must be no vague generalities. The reader is primarily interested in facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize concrete information (works performed, performers, venue, notable occurrences), keep subjective impressions tightly linked to observable facts, and avoid unsupported evaluative generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate technical musical comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the enjoyment of any art is both emotional and intelligent ... the ideal student reporter of musical events is one who has some knowledge of music as well as of journalism. He should be able to infuse just enough technical comment into his story to give it reality, just as the sports writer uses enough of the vernacular to make his account live for the enthusiast as well as for the reader who has no technical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise technical remarks (tempo, phrasing, balance, ensemble accuracy) to lend credibility for knowledgeable readers while keeping language accessible for general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply news-writing principles for straight-news musical reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever specific information from the program will interest readers, should be presented. The principles of news writing hold if the report is straight news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting performances as news, use inverted-pyramid clarity: lead with the most important facts (what, who, where, when, significance), then add supporting details and quotes; avoid feature-style meandering when a news report is required.
